info.album: Be My Baby / Baby, I Love You

podcast.body: This song had a profound impact on Brian Wilson upon its release, so much so that he recalled having to pull over his car when he first heard its drum intro. He obsessively played the record on repeat for days, diligently studying every nuance of its production, and it served as the direct inspiration for The Beach Boys' "Don't Worry Baby." "It had originally been intended for the run-et, and was inspired by being my baby, which had astonished Brian Wilson when it had been released a few months earlier."

srcs.source: A History of Rock Music in 500 Songs
srcs.episode: Episode 117: "Don't Worry Baby" by the Beach Boys

podcast.body: The group's breakout hit and first number one, primarily written by Jeff Barry and Ellie Greenwich, with a likely contribution to the verse-chorus transition from Phil Spector. Ronnie recorded the lead vocals over three days at Gold Star Studios in Los Angeles, while backing vocals were provided by The Blossoms, Sonny Bono, and Cher, not the other Ronettes. The track is famously characterized by Hal Blaine's simple yet powerful drum intro, recorded with a distinctive sound by engineer Larry Levine. "The song that eventually became the group's first hit, Be My Baby, was mostly written by one of the many husband and wife songwriting teams that had developed at the Royal Building, Jeff Barry and Dalley Gvennich."
